name: op_resize_no_dom_rebuild
description: THE RESIZE POLICY (user ruling 2026-08-08, harvested-breakpoints revision 2026-08-10): a resize NEVER re-invokes the app's layout() — dom_regenerations stays 0 — unless it crosses a boundary the callback can observe: a HARVESTED viewport breakpoint (an @media bound or inline ViewportWidth/Height condition actually present in the DOM — the old hardcoded CSS_BREAKPOINTS guess list is gone; it both missed real widget thresholds like the ribbon's 720px AND fired ~66ms regenerations on every drag across 640/768/1024), an orientation flip, or a recorded window_width_*/window_height_* query answer. This scenario's stylesheet declares ONE @media bound at 1000px: 800->900->850 crosses nothing (including the old guess list's 768/1024 — that is the point) and must regenerate ZERO times; 850->1100 crosses the declared 1000px bound and must regenerate EXACTLY ONCE. Background: a Wayland drag delivers one configure PER PIXEL (373 measured in 5 s) and each full regeneration cost 654-942 ms, so the pre-fix pipeline could repaint ~1.4x/second during a drag.
